subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
lesson: Unit 2 – Lesson 7: English in action – Asking for help
outcomes: I can ask for help politely with a technology task.
I can answer when someone asks me for help.
I can say the weak form of to /tə/ in questions.

tf.s: “Could you show me how to use this?” is more polite than “Show me how to use this!”
tf.why: Starting with Could you … makes a request polite.

tf.s: In the dialogue, the girl wants to print her English homework.
tf.why: Yes, she needs help to print her English homework.

tf.s: Mum helps the girl revise for her exam before dinner.
tf.why: Mum has to cook dinner, so she can help after dinner.

tf.s: “Of course.” is a way to say yes when someone asks for help.
tf.why: Of course means yes, I can help you.

tf.s: “Sorry, not now.” means you are happy to help right away.
tf.why: Sorry, not now means you cannot help at this moment.

tf.s: In “I need to go online”, the word to is usually short and weak: /tə/.
tf.why: In connected speech, to often sounds short, like /tə/.

tf.s: In “Can you show me how to do it?”, the word to is the stressed word.
tf.why: We stress show and do, not the small word to.

tf.s: “Help me with my homework.” is a polite question.
tf.why: It is an order; Could you help me with my homework, please? is polite.

tf.s: To turn on the printer, the girl presses a button.
tf.why: Right, she presses that button to turn it on.

tf.s: “Do you have time to …?” is a way to ask for help.
tf.why: Yes, Do you have time to help me? is a polite question for help.

boxes.q: Complete: Can you show me ___ to turn it on?
boxes.why: We say show me how to do something.

boxes.q: Complete: You need ___ type the password.
boxes.why: need is followed by to + verb.

boxes.q: Which word starts a polite request?
boxes.why: Could you …? is a polite way to ask.

boxes.q: Why can’t Mum help the girl now?
boxes.why: Mum is busy cooking dinner, so she helps later.

boxes.q: Which reply means “I can help you”?
boxes.why: Of course is a friendly yes.

boxes.q: How does to sound in “Do you have time to help me?”
boxes.why: In a quick question, to is weak and short.

boxes.q: Which reply means “It is not difficult”?
boxes.why: It’s easy! tells the person the task is simple.

boxes.q: Complete: Please can I ___ your laptop?
boxes.why: After can I we use the base verb: use.

boxes.q: Which question asks for help with technology?
o: Can you show me how to upload a photo?
boxes.why: Uploading a photo is a technology task.

boxes.q: When can Mum help the girl revise?
boxes.why: Mum says she can help after dinner.

hunt.q: Can you show me ___ to do it?
A friendly yes to a request
What does the girl want to print?
Mum can help her revise ___ dinner.
The weak form of to sounds like…
She presses a ___ to turn it on.
Do you have ___ to help me?

mcq.q: What does the girl ask her mum to help with?
o: Printing her English homework and revising for an exam
mcq.why: She needs help to print her homework and revise for an exam.

mcq.q: Which of these is a response, not a question?
o: Do you have time to help me?
Can you show me how to …?
mcq.why: Sorry, not now. is an answer to a request.

mcq.q: Which words are stressed in “Can you show me how to do it?”
mcq.why: Important words like show and do are stressed; to is weak.

mcq.q: Which question uses the language from the lesson to ask for help?
o: Do you have time to help me?
mcq.why: Do you have time to …? is one of the help questions.

mcq.q: Make it polite: “Help me with my homework.”
o: Could you help me with my homework, please?
You help me with my homework now.
Did you help me with my homework?
mcq.why: Could you … please? turns an order into a polite request.

mcq.q: You want to download an app but you don’t know how. What do you say?
o: Can you show me how to download this app?
Where did you download it yesterday?
mcq.why: Can you show me how to …? asks for help politely.

mcq.q: A: Do you have time to help me? B: Sorry, not now. What can A say next?
o: Could you help me after dinner?
Thank you for helping me now.
mcq.why: If the person is busy, you can politely ask for help later.

mcq.q: Why is “Could you show me how to use this?” better than “Show me how to use this!”?
o: It is a polite question, not an order.
mcq.why: A polite question sounds kind and respectful.

mcq.q: Which word is weak and short in “I need to go online”?
mcq.why: Small words like to are weak; need, go and online carry the meaning.

mcq.q: Mum says she has to cook dinner. What does this tell us?
o: She is busy now but can help later.
She doesn’t want to help at all.
She thinks the homework is easy.
mcq.why: Mum is busy now, so she offers to help after dinner.
